content.text:
Based on the official Brussels sources, here's a comprehensive answer to your situation:

## 1. Is it mandatory? Exemptions

Yes — for someone matching your exact profile, the programme is mandatory. According to the official Brussels city portal, you are **obliged to follow the "parcours d'accueil"** if you meet all three criteria:

citations.cited_text:
Une personne est **obligée de suivre le parcours** si elle :

- est inscrite pour la première fois au registre des étrangers d'une commune bruxelloise...
citations.title: Parcours d'accueil obligatoire à Bruxelles

content.text: a person is obliged to follow the course if she is registered for the first time in the register of foreigners of a Brussels municipality with a residence permit of more than 3 months, is between 18 and 65 years old, and has legally resided in Belgium for less than 3 years.

Since you are 40, registering for the first time with a permit valid over three months, and have resided legally for less than three years, the obligation applies to you.

**Exemptions** exist for certain categories:

citations.cited_text:
Ce parcours d'accueil consiste en :

Le primo-arrivant peut cependant bénéficier d'une **exemption** si, par exemple, il vient d'un pays de l'Union Eu...
citations.title: L’intégration des primo-arrivants

content.text: a newcomer can however benefit from an exemption if, for example, they come from a European Union country, or if they have already obtained an integration certificate
. More broadly,

citations.cited_text: Les citoyens d'un État-membre de l'Union européennes (UE), de l’Espace économique européen (EEE), de la Suisse et des membres de leur famille sont aus...
citations.title: Parcours d'accueil ou d'intégration et aides pour migrants

content.text: citizens of an EU member state, the European Economic Area, Switzerland and their family members are also considered "primo-arrivants" under the Brussels French-speaking decree
, though EU/EEA/Swiss nationals are typically exempt from the obligation itself (only non-EU citizens like you are generally subject to the mandatory track). If you are exempt,

citations.cited_text: Dans ce cas, il peut toujours suivre un parcours d'accueil sur base volontaire.
citations.title: L’intégration des primo-arrivants

content.text: you can still follow a welcome programme on a voluntary basis

.

## 2. Which authority/office to contact

Since 1 January 2024, the French-speaking track is managed by Vivalis (formerly COCOF/COCOM), while the Dutch-speaking track is run by BON (Brussels Onthaalbureau voor Nieuwkomers).

citations.cited_text:
Pour suivre un parcours d'accueil, le primo-arrivant doit s'adresser à l'un des bureaux d'accueil agréés à Bruxelles :

**En français :**

- BAPA BXL ...
citations.title: Parcours d'accueil obligatoire à Bruxelles

content.text: To follow a welcome programme, the newcomer must contact one of the approved welcome offices in Brussels: in French, BAPA BXL in Brussels, BAPA Convivial in Forest, or BAPA VIA in Molenbeek or Schaerbeek; in Dutch, BON in Brussels, Schaerbeek or Anderlecht.

Your municipality (commune) will typically first notify you of the obligation when you register.

## 3. Registration and completion deadlines

- **Registration deadline:**

citations.cited_text: Les primo-arrivants concernés doivent s'inscrire dans un bureau d'accueil dans les six mois suivant la notification de leur obligation par leur commun...
citations.title: 7 631 primo-arrivants suivent actuellement un parcours d'accueil ...

content.text: Primo-arrivants concerned must register at a welcome office within six months following notification of their obligation by their municipality.
- **Completion deadline:**

citations.cited_text: Depuis juin 2022, ce parcours d’accueil est accessible aux personnes étrangères et il est obligatoire pour les personnes primo-arrivantes, qui doivent...
citations.title: Parcours d'accueil - Positions du CIRÉ

content.text: the welcome programme is mandatory for primo-arrivants, who must complete it within a period of 18 months.

Completion is achieved through regular participation in each component of the training programme, rather than passing an exam.

## 4. Choice of French or Dutch pathway

Yes, you have free choice of language track.

citations.cited_text: Het samenwerkingsakkoord is aangepast naar aanleiding van de goedgekeurde ordonnantie van de Verenigde Vergadering, waardoor nieuwkomers in het tweeta...
citations.title: Verplicht inburgeringstraject nieuwkomers Brussel-Hoofdstad: ontwerp ...

content.text: Newcomers in the bilingual Brussels-Capital territory now have the choice between a bilingual welcome programme managed by the Gemeenschappelijke Gemeenschapscommissie (Vivalis/GGC) or a Dutch-language programme
run by BON. This free-choice principle was recently reaffirmed:

citations.cited_text: Le principe du libre choix du primo-arrivant, tel qu'il est consacré par l'ordonnance du 20 juillet 2023, demeure toutefois le point de départ. Il n'e...
citations.title: Plus de 16.000 primo-arrivants ont pris part au parcours d'accueil ...

content.text: the principle of free choice by the newcomer, as enshrined in the ordinance of 20 July 2023, remains the starting point — it is not possible to impose on a person the choice of an office under the Dutch-speaking system
, even if that system has more available capacity. In practice, waiting lists currently exist on the French-speaking (Vivalis/BAPA) side due to high demand, but as someone under mandatory obligation,

citations.cited_text: Des listes d'attente sont donc utilisées pour les participants non soumis à l'obligation, ce qui n'est pas le cas des primo-arrivants obligatoires.
citations.title: Plus de 16.000 primo-arrivants ont pris part au parcours d'accueil ...

content.text: waiting lists are used for participants not subject to the obligation, which is not the case for mandatory primo-arrivants

— meaning you should be prioritized for placement regardless of which track you choose.

## 5. Program content and current official sources

The programme itself includes:

citations.title: Du neuf pour le Parcours d’accueil des primo-arrivants à Bruxelles ...

content.text: socio-administrative support, language courses, a 10-hour module on rights and duties in Belgium, and a 50-hour citizenship training module covering Belgian history and migration, geography, institutional functioning, the labor market and social security system.

**Official sources:**
- Vivalis (regional health/social authority managing the French/bilingual track): vivalis.brussels — pages on "Inburgeringstraject" and "L'intégration des primo-arrivants"
- City of Brussels official portal: bruxelles.be — "Parcours d'accueil obligatoire à Bruxelles"
- Legal basis: Ordinance of 11 May 2017 (COCOM) and the amending Ordinance of 20 July 2023; Cooperation Agreement of 20 December 2018 (amended 7 March 2024) between the Flemish Community, French Community Commission, and Common Community Commission
- CBAI (Brussels Centre for Intercultural Action): cbai.be — "L'accueil des primo-arrivants"

**Practical note:** Given current demand pressures (over 13,000 people were under active obligation as of mid-2026, per Vivalis), I'd recommend registering with a BAPA or BON office as soon as possible after your municipal registration to secure your spot within the 6-month registration window.
